objective: Converge the pinned stock PyTorch 2.11.0+cu126 torch.cuda CPU profile, then qualify the same canonical Kernel IR corpus on the AMD RADV/Vulkan backend with explicit backend completion and process-level activation, without PyTorch source, wheel, or API changes; broader application claims require their own declared acceptance scope.

lanes.outcome: Run pinned stock PyTorch through import, driver enumeration, runtime copy, artifact intake, and eager add using the normal torch.cuda API, with eager add completed by a daemon submission on the CPU backend.
acceptance: The checked-in gate provisions pinned stock PyTorch 2.11.0+cu126 and reaches all five baseline stages without modifying PyTorch source, wheel contents, or torch.cuda APIs; MetaFlux package, launcher, and loader-environment activation remain allowed.
The exact baseline-required Driver and internal-table surface, minimal neutral request schema and lifetime, and daemon CPU execution mode plus cache identity are closed before integration.
Eager add produces an observed daemon submission and CPU-backend completion; the CUDA provider performs no tensor arithmetic, result materialization, or false-success shortcut.

lanes.outcome: Broaden the baseline into a versioned PyTorch CUDA CPU profile with a complete provider-surface matrix, handle-negative coverage, canonical neutral request and Kernel IR boundaries, and a backend-executed operator corpus.
acceptance: The Driver and profile-specific internal-table matrix classifies the full pinned surface, and invalid, stale, destroyed, cross-module, reuse, and teardown handle cases pass.
The versioned neutral framework-kernel request and canonical Kernel IR boundary carry no CUDA, PyTorch, MLIR, LLVM, Vulkan, or target-specific wire types.

Every accepted row in the frozen CPU corpus has canonical Kernel IR semantics and passes interpreter, cold JIT, warm JIT, and AOT with per-request executor evidence, mode-appropriate provenance and cache identity, and stable errors; operation-specific daemon CPU branches do not establish generic interpreter or compiled coverage.
The closed library-backed matmul boundary is retained; broader dtype, shape, layout, batching, and library configurations require explicit corpus and negative-test coverage before acceptance.

lanes.outcome: Qualify the same versioned PyTorch CUDA Kernel IR corpus on an explicitly selected AMD RADV/Vulkan context, with real device submission/completion, CPU differential evidence, lifecycle behavior, and process-level activation.
acceptance: The Vulkan route decision is closed before implementing the qualifying route; the existing optional adapter is unqualified. Each context fixes its backend before resource success, with no per-kernel CPU fallback or CPU-native shortcut in Vulkan qualification.

The first GPU slice proves unchanged stock PyTorch eager add, copy and readback on the named physical AMD RADV device, including device identity and correlated GPU submission/completion; the full accepted Kernel IR corpus then lowers directly through target-constrained MLIR/SPIR-V without an LLVM detour.
Stream, event, allocator, multi-stream, synchronization, teardown, and daemon-loss rows pass for the pinned client on the Vulkan daemon route.

CPU and Vulkan execute the same corpus manifest with bit-exact differential evidence, current baseline/frontier gap manifests, and green cumulative v0.1.x regression; missing physical GPU execution is not a qualification pass.

The declared corpus runs through one process-level activation entry without PyTorch changes or test-only orchestration. Any additional model, training, mixed-precision, or compiled-framework claim first closes its exact application scope and acceptance evidence; Intel and physical NVIDIA/dual-driver gates remain v2 scope.
